flawed_step: Assuming E[X_{n+1}|X_n]=X_n implies E[X_{n+1}|X_1,...,X_n]=X_n; conditioning on the current value alone can average out dependence on the past.
counterexample: Four equally likely outcomes (X1,X2,X3): (1,2,2), (1,0,1), (-1,0,-1), (-1,-2,-2). Then E[X2|X1=1]=(2+0)/2=1, E[X2|X1=-1]=(0-2)/2=-1; E[X3|X2=2]=2, E[X3|X2=-2]=-2, E[X3|X2=0]=(1-1)/2=0. So both Markov-style conditions hold, all variables are bounded. But on {X1=1,X2=0} (prob 1/4), E[X3|F_2]=1 ≠ 0=X2, so it is not a martingale w.r.t. the natural filtration.
assessment_summary: Explicit finite counterexample: the X2=0 state mixes paths coming from X1=1 and X1=-1, and X3 remembers X1. E[X3|X2]=X2 holds, but E[X3|X1,X2]≠X2.
